done_when: When the only failed required check is a review check that ran before the branch's latest commit, close re-runs that job once and waits for it.

known.title: Not done: Retry and wait for the only failed required review from an older commit
Functional: A current-head review can be mistaken for an old review
Test: Retry and wait for the only failed required review from an older commit
Functional: The repair rejects stale reviews whose runs report the base SHA

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 4
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - the failed required review links to a run that reviewed commit A, and the branch has advanced to commit B.
A `pull_request_target` workflow run can report the base commit C as `head_sha`. The new lookup checks C for the linked job URL, but `.github/workflows/forge.yml:180-195` posts that status to the event's pull-request head A. The URL is therefore absent from C's statuses, so close returns without requesting the retry. The previous code did not require this lookup, making the repair break the named retry path for this GitHub response. This is new evidence relevant to the ruling to verify the commit the review actually checked: the workflow run's `head_sha` is not necessarily that commit.
findings.title: Functional: The repair rejects stale reviews whose runs report the base SHA

why: A review check that failed before a CI fix stays failed until someone re-runs that job by hand, so close keeps reporting a failed check after the cause is fixed.
